transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Time: 14:30 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Goldcrest Head of AI), James O'Neil (Goldcrest CTO), Priya Shah (Goldcrest DevOps)
Links shared: pricing deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/goldcrest-renewal), security summary (https://redwood.ai/security/goldcrest), benchmark sheet (link to spreadsheet)

Summary:
Quick renewal and expansion check-in to discuss Dedicated capacity upgrade, adding EU and APAC regions, and timing for contract extension. Agreed to run latency/cost benchmarks and produce updated pricing. Possible Private/VPC scoping if KMS/HSM and data residency requirement is strict.

Topics:
- Current usage and pain: prefixes caching, burst capacity needs, token spikes during peak routing windows
- Dedicated vs Hosted for predictable throughput and cost modeling
- Regions: request to add eu-west and ap-southeast for customer facing endpoints
- Contract extension term (12 vs 24 months) and pricing breakpoints
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 questions (brief)

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - Samira from Redwood, Daniel, and on the Goldcrest side?
[00:08] Marta: Hi, Marta here.
[00:10] James: James, hi.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, hi.
[00:15] Samira: Great. The objective for today's call is to walk through renewal options and the expansion asks - more capacity and additional regions - and make sure we have next steps to land the contract amendment. 
[00:28] Marta: Yep that sounds right. We're seeing big spikes when shipments batch overnight and the hosted plan is getting... we've hit burst limits a few times and the latency jitter is hurting the routing service.
[00:40] Daniel: Can you say roughly how big the spikes are? tokens per minute, or concurrent requests?
[00:45] Marta: Ballpark 2.2 million tokens in a 10 minute window during peak - it's a sudden spike from the planning pipeline. We also want eu-west for our EU ops and ap-southeast as we expand in SEA.
[00:57] Samira: Okay that's helpful. For predictable throughput we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated with a reserved GPU pool - that avoids burst throttle and gives predictable p99s. There are a couple levers: committed throughput, burst buffer, and autoscale policies.
[01:12] James: We'd like some numbers. What would, say, a 2x capacity upgrade look like cost-wise and what are p99 latencies?
[01:20] Samira: I'll send a pricing sheet with the 2x and 3x rows. From our benchmarks on similar customers, Dedicated pools on A100/RTX-class hardware give p50 ~40-60ms and p99 under 220-300ms depending on prompt length and batching. Those are approximate but we can run a custom benchmark.
[01:38] Priya: And for regions - do we replicate state or route? Our compliance folks demand EU data residency for EU customers.
[01:45] Daniel: We support region-local routing and optional KV cache replication. For strict residency we recommend running a Dedicated pool in eu-west with data pinned there; for lower-risk routing we can route EU traffic to eu-west but keep global cache in a primary region.
[02:01] Marta: Replication might be heavy. If we run two Dedicated pools, what's the extra cost and how does failover work?
[02:08] Daniel: Cost is additive - you're reserving GPU capacity in two regions. Failover is policy-based: by default we prefer local region, and we can set an automatic fallback to a nearby region only if local capacity is saturated. We also support synchronous KV replication for small state, but large KV sets will increase bandwidth/cost.
[02:25] James: What's the onboarding time for a new region? Weeks? Days?
[02:28] Samira: For hosted regions it's typically 2-3 business days to schedule capacity; Dedicated can be provisioned in 1-2 weeks depending on availability. If you need private/on-prem, that adds a few weeks for packaging and security review.
[02:40] Priya: Our security team asked about KMS/HSM integration and audit logs - do you have references?
[02:45] Samira: Yes we've shared the security summary link in the chat. We support customer-managed KMS, bring-your-own-key, and detailed audit logs. We'll attach SOC2 artifacts as well.
[02:55] Marta: Great. About the contract - we were thinking of extending to 24 months if there's a discount for multi-region commitment.
[03:00] Samira: We can offer a tiered discount: a 12-month renewal with standard renewal pricing or a 24-month commit with discounted reserved capacity rates and region add-on discounts. I'll put concrete numbers in the pricing doc.
[03:12] James: Any blockers around our compliance? We do have some constrained endpoints behind a VPC.
[03:16] Daniel: VPC/private deployment is supported; for cross-vpc connectivity we can do peering or VPN. Some customers run a private control plane with our on-prem connectors for air-gapped segments. There's more lift there but it's doable.
[03:29] Marta: Okay sounds good. I also want a simple TCO comparison between expanding hosted with burst vs moving to Dedicated with caching.
[03:36] Samira: We'll include that in the spreadsheet - per-token cost, committed GPU hours, expected savings from prefix caching and quantization recommendations.
[03:44] Priya: For the benchmark, can Daniel include both text-gen and embedding workloads? We use embeddings for matching and text-gen for summarization.
[03:51] Daniel: Yes we'll run both. I'll include sequence length distributions you use; Marta if you can drop the sample prompt set in the sheet that will help.
[03:58] Marta: I'll upload a sample prompt set after this call.
[04:02] Samira: Great. Next steps recap - Samira to send pricing; Daniel to run region benchmarks; Goldcrest to confirm residency requirements and upload prompts; target to have revised contract draft the following week.
[04:15] James: That works. Any other questions?
[04:18] Priya: One quick thing - do you have a break-fix SLA for Dedicated?
[04:22] Samira: Yes Dedicated comes with SLA tiers. We'll include SLA table in the amendment; higher SLAs include faster incident response and credits.
[04:30] Marta: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[04:33] Samira: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the doc and benchmark link.
[04:36] (call ends)
